react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on galactose metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in the treatment group. RaMP multi-DB ORA (merged SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) ranks Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182, FDR = 1.72 × 10⁻¹²) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:map00052, FDR = 1.72 × 10⁻¹²) as the top two hits, driven by five input metabolites: galactitol (C01697), myo-inositol (C00137), galactinol (C01235), sucrose (C00089), and glycerol (C00116). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) as its top hit (p = 5.16 × 10⁻⁸), with the identical five compound overlaps. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis ranks Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p = 0.016) at position 5, again with the same five carbohydrate members plus D-glucose and inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate. This three-paradigm consensus — FDR < 10⁻¹² (RaMP), p < 10⁻⁷ (MetaboAnalystR), and p = 0.016 (Mummichog) — establishes robust, annotation-independent support. The driver carbohydrates span the Leloir pathway: galactinol (the galactosyl donor to myo-inositol), galactitol (the sorbitol-side oxidation product), and sucrose (an upstream disaccharide), while glycerol appears as a shared intermediate with glycerophospholipid metabolism, consistent with the secondary RaMP hit WP:WP2533 (Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway, FDR = 2.6 × 10⁻⁵) that also features myo-inositol and ethanolamine. Dopamine and 2-methoxyestradiol are not enriched in the carbohydrate cluster; instead they connect to distinct, lower-significance pathways (GPCR downstream signalling via dopamine; androgen and estrogen biosynthesis via 2-methoxyestradiol in the mummichog hit). Squalene independently maps to steroid biosynthesis. The dominant biological story is therefore a coordinated perturbation of galactose utilisation and its intersection with phospholipid head-group metabolism, rather than a discrete neurotransmitter or sterol effect.
